nodes.falsz_ok.text.t: Hauk looks at you for a long time, then checks something on his map and nods. "Under the fort. I figured they weren't stupid enough to use the ford." You get fifty groats as a deposit. "The rest when the wagons burn." You won't see the rest. But today an imperial crossbow is waiting under the fort, and the captain will probably appreciate someone herding men into his sights.

nodes.falsz_zle.text.t: Hauk smiles and goes on greasing his boot. "Under the fort? My scout lay under that fort three nights and saw two hares. You lie well, there's practice behind it, but do it once more and the lads with the handguns come for you. Now you get a second chance at the truth. Not everyone gets this offer."

nodes.nie.text.t: "Your own." Hauk repeats it as if tasting it. "Your own haven't paid you in three months, but fine, I respect that. The offer stands as long as the war does. So, a long time."

nodes.prawda.text.t: Hauk puts down the rag and writes two words on a scrap of bark. He counts out the silver without haggling, which is the worst sign. "Good doing business with you. The men with the wagons probably wouldn't agree, but nobody asked them."

nodes.proch_ok.text.t: You leave out the back, as you said. Behind the tent stand powder barrels under a tarp, and a bit further off a bucket. There are two buckets and nine barrels, but the bungs sit loose, and the sentry is just telling a story about his wife. By the time he finishes, the powder in nine barrels is wet mush. Nobody will notice until the first volley.

nodes.proch_zle.text.t: Your hand is already on a bung when the sentry stops talking about his wife. He looks at you, you look at him, and the barrel looks at both of you. You say you're looking for the privy. The sentry points the other way, not taking his other hand off the handgun. From the tent Hauk calls: "Come back and let's talk like men, because barrels don't take apologies."

nodes.s.options.[falsz].text.t: The Old Road under the fort, every third day.

nodes.s.options.[nie].text.t: I don't sell out my own.

nodes.s.options.[prawda].text.t: At night, across the ford. No guard.

nodes.s.options.[proch].text.t: I'll think about it. I'm leaving out the back, past your powder.

nodes.s.text.t: A fair-bearded sotnik sits in the tent greasing his boots as if that were the most important thing in this war. He doesn't reach for a weapon. "You're not a prisoner, you'd be tied up. You're not a deserter, you'd stink of fear. So you've come to earn. Hauk. I care about one thing: which way the powder wagons go to Crow Mountain. I pay ninety groats, in silver, no receipt."
